title: Valuation convergence of deep p-adic logarithm and exponential series
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension as in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_E$, normalized valuation $v_E(\mathfrak m_E)=1$ and $e=v_E(\ell)$. Use the extended absolute value $|z|_E=\ell^{-v_E(z)/e}$ for $z\ne0$. For every integer $r>e/(\ell-1)$ put $\delta=r-e/(\ell-1)>0$, $q=\ell^{-r/e}$ and $\theta=\ell^{-\delta/e}<1$. For every integer $n\ge1$,
$$v_\ell(n)\le\frac{n-1}{\ell-1},\qquad v_\ell(n!)\le\frac{n-1}{\ell-1}.$$
For every $x\in\mathfrak m_E^r$,
$$v_E(x^n/n)\ge nr-e v_\ell(n)\ge r+(n-1)\delta,\qquad v_E(x^n/n!)\ge nr-e v_\ell(n!)\ge r+(n-1)\delta.$$
Equivalently the two coefficient sequences satisfy
$$|1/n|_E q^n\le q\theta^{n-1},\qquad |1/n!|_E q^n\le q\theta^{n-1}\quad(n\ge1).$$
The series $L(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}(-1)^{n+1}x^n/n$ and $A(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}x^n/n!$ converge uniformly on $\mathfrak m_E^r=\{x:|x|_E\le q\}$. Their sums lie in $\mathfrak m_E^r$, and both maps are continuous there. Thus $\log(1+x)=L(x)$ and $\exp(x)=1+A(x)$ converge uniformly on these domains, with logarithm in $\mathfrak m_E^r$ and exponential in $1+\mathfrak m_E^r$.
